caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Chile started the period as the region's fiscal exemplar: debt was just 5% of GDP in 2006 and 3.9% in 2007, the trough, as the structural-balance rule turned copper windfalls into sovereign wealth savings. It has risen in nearly every year since as the rule was relaxed and spending grew: 11.9% in 2012, 17.4% in 2015, 25.8% in 2018, 28.3% in 2019, 32.4% in 2020 on COVID outlays, 39.4% in 2023, 41.7% in 2024, and a projected 41.8% in 2025. Dollar GDP nearly tripled from $153.8bn in 2006 to a projected $355.4bn in 2025, so the rise is a policy choice, not a collapse. Debt remains moderate by global standards, but the trajectory - an eightfold ratio increase in under two decades - is why the copper stabilization funds and a credible fiscal path back to balance dominate the policy debate.
inflation_management: Chile's inflation-targeting central bank (3% target, among the world's oldest adopters) kept inflation mostly between 1.4% and 4.7% through 2021, with brief excursions to 8.7% in 2008 (commodity spike) and lows of 1.4-1.5% in 2009-2010. The pandemic response broke the calm: three rounds of AFP pension-fund withdrawals flooded the economy with liquidity while supply chains seized, pushing inflation to 4.5% in 2021 and 11.6% in 2022, the series high. The central bank responded with one of the region's most aggressive tightening cycles, and inflation fell to 7.6% in 2023, 3.9% in 2024, and a projected 4.2% in 2025 - essentially back at target. The episode demonstrated both the cost of fiscal indiscipline and the credibility the bank had banked over two decades.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis; inflation spiked to 8.7% in 2008 then collapsed to 1.5% in 2009.
Massive February earthquake; reconstruction spending helped the copper-boom recovery.
Tax and education reforms under Bachelet's second government.
Estallido social: mass protests from October 2019 over inequality forced a constitutional process.
COVID-19; pension-fund withdrawals supercharged a demand boom.
Gabriel Boric won the presidency (Dec 2021); first constitutional draft rejected in Sept 2022.
Second constitutional draft rejected in December, closing the constitutional chapter.
Hard-right Jose Antonio Kast won the Dec 14, 2025 runoff with 58.2%; inflation projected at 4.2%.

outlook_next_decade: Chile enters the next decade macroeconomically sound - inflation at target, moderate debt, copper still structural - but politically transformed, with its most right-wing president since the dictatorship taking office in 2026. The base case is pro-market deregulation, faster mining permits, and a renewed push for growth after years of constitutional distraction. The open questions are whether crime and immigration pressures produce policy overreach, and whether copper revenues fund tax relief or the long-delayed pension and fiscal consolidation. The institutional guardrails (independent central bank, fiscal rule) have survived every stress test so far; their survival under Kast is the decade's key variable.
